leading_positions.synthesis: Five of six members propose B049 as a single-part prize with the same trio, Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, with citations centred on GLP-1 physiology and the biologically active peptide as the basis for incretin-based therapy. They share the view that the discovery is mature and independently confirmed and that clinical benefit is supported by large randomised trials. They differ in how explicitly the citation should name the therapies (Perlmann and Svenningsson would state incretin-based therapy openly; Linnarsson and El-Manira frame it as what the physiology enabled) and in how firmly they hold the Mojsov seat: El-Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann and Svenningsson each say they could accept Knudsen in that seat if the committee decides to recognise drug development, while Perlmann also wants the priority question settled first.

Sandberg also proposes B049 as a single-part prize but with Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, arguing that the citation should span physiology through to the design of long-acting analogues and that Knudsen's contribution is the least disputed in the historical record. This position shares Drucker and Holst and the ballot with the other five, and differs only in the third seat. Sandberg states that Knudsen's slot is the weakest if the committee decides discovery rather than development should decide the trio, and that he would not block a Mojsov trio in that case.

areas_of_agreement: All six members ranked B049 first at the opening and all six prefer B049 as their round-1 configuration, each stating that the case rests on merit and not on the unanimity itself.

All six configurations contain Drucker and Holst, and none proposes adding a second prize part to B049; Linnarsson explicitly prefers a single-part prize, and El-Manira, Perlmann and Svenningsson see no clean way to fit a second achievement within three names.

All six name B014 (CAR-T) as an alternative, and the members who discuss its composition (El-Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg, Svenningsson and Wahren-Herlenius) favour June and Sadelain without Rosenberg, whose adoptive cell therapy work is treated as a distinct line.

All members acknowledge that attribution, not scientific merit, is the main weakness of the leading ballot, and several say they rely on recollection of the priority history rather than verified primary documents.
No member discloses a conflict with any credited candidate on the shortlist.
scientific_disputes: Whether B049 should be framed as a physiology-and-active-peptide discovery (five members) or as physiology through to the engineering of long-acting analogues (Sandberg), and whether acylation-based half-life extension is a conceptually new scientific step (Sandberg) or pharmaceutical optimisation of an existing mechanism (El-Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann).

Whether the Prize should reward the insight that changed a field or the clinical demonstration that it works in patients: Perlmann and Wahren-Herlenius apply this to GLP-1 versus CAR-T, and Wahren-Herlenius asks for a consistent discovery-versus-development standard across GLP-1, imatinib and CAR-T.

Whether B021 (optogenetics) is a discovery of molecular biology (channelrhodopsin as a light-gated channel) or a tool whose main impact is in circuit neuroscience, and whether a tool needs to meet a clinical bar; El-Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann and Wahren-Herlenius each place it as an alternative or below B014 on these grounds.

Whether conceptual clarity of mechanism can justify ranking basic-science candidates such as B023 (unfolded protein response; Svenningsson's alternative) and B001 (TOR; Sandberg's alternative) alongside therapeutic candidates, given that their clinical consequences are less direct; Perlmann and Wahren-Herlenius argue they are mature but indirect.
attribution_disputes: Third seat in B049: Mojsov (El-Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann, Svenningsson, Wahren-Herlenius) versus Knudsen (Sandberg), with Habener, who is outside the credited names, also raised as a contributor to proglucagon and GLP-1 biology by El-Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg, Svenningsson and Wahren-Herlenius.

Mojsov's priority for the active truncated GLP-1 is described as disputed by all six members; Sandberg locates the dispute in overlap with Habener's group, while Svenningsson and Wahren-Herlenius describe it as a dispute of degree that should be tested against the primary literature.

B014 (CAR-T): the credited names are June, Sadelain and Rosenberg, but El-Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg, Svenningsson and Wahren-Herlenius point to Eshhar, with Wahren-Herlenius also naming Kuwana and Gross, as originators of the chimeric receptor concept who are outside the supplied credit; the members agree Rosenberg belongs to a separate lineage but disagree on how much the Eshhar gap weakens the ballot.

B021 (optogenetics): six credited names cannot be reduced to three without excluding a central contributor; El-Manira's trio (Deisseroth, Nagel, Hegemann) and Perlmann's trio (Bamberg, Nagel, Hegemann) differ, and Linnarsson and Wahren-Herlenius say either choice leaves out Bamberg, Boyden, Miesenboeck or Deisseroth.

B047 (HPV vaccines), discussed in responses only: Jian Zhou's death and unresolved priority between the NCI and Frazer groups are cited by El-Manira, Perlmann and Wahren-Herlenius as complicating a three-name split.
maturity_disputes: B049 is treated as mature by all members after decades of independent confirmation and randomised outcome trials; El-Manira alone adds that long-term safety and durability are still accumulating, without seeing this as affecting the discovery case.

B014 is described as less settled than B049 because of low cure rates in solid tumours and an evolving toxicity profile (El-Manira, Perlmann, Wahren-Herlenius), while Wahren-Herlenius sees the autoimmune extension as strengthening its case.

B021 and B023: patient benefit or therapeutic consequence is described as early or modest (El-Manira, Perlmann, Svenningsson, Wahren-Herlenius), while Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius describe cGAS-STING (B022) as mechanistically clear but early because STING-directed therapies have not delivered.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: No member reports a conflict with a credited candidate on the shortlist.

Svenningsson (chair) discloses a postdoctoral period with Paul Greengard and about twenty co-authored works with Perlmann on dopamine neurons, Nurr1 and autophagy (unaudited count); neither involves a credited candidate. Perlmann also notes past co-authorship with Svenningsson and El-Manira as not bearing on these candidates.

Linnarsson discloses eight co-authored works with Sandberg and other co-authors (Castelo-Branco, Betsholtz, Ernfors, Frisen, Lundeberg, Kharchenko); Sandberg notes co-authorship with Linnarsson and Frisen; none is a credited candidate or a shortlisted topic.

El-Manira discloses an interest in optogenetics as a tool for motor-circuit research but no tie to a credited name; Wahren-Herlenius notes that her field of autoimmunity is adjacent to the CAR-T autoimmune extension and cGAS-STING, with no documented tie to a candidate; Perlmann discloses collaboration with Ronald Evans and Johan Ericson, neither credited on the shortlist.
questions_for_round2: For B049, should the third seat go to Mojsov or Knudsen, and what documentary evidence on priority for the active GLP-1 peptide, including the role of Habener's group, can the members cite from primary sources rather than recollection?

Should the B049 citation recognise physiology and the active peptide only, or explicitly also cover the long-acting therapies, and would a decision for the latter change which of Mojsov or Knudsen is credited?

Is B049 intended as a single-part prize, as Linnarsson states and others imply, or does any member wish to pair it with a second achievement such as B014, and if so which three-name split would avoid weakening the GLP-1 attribution?
If B014 is pursued, how should the citation handle Eshhar's absence from the credited names, and does the June and Sadelain pair stand without Rosenberg?
What discovery-versus-development standard should be applied consistently to B049, B014 and imatinib (B011), as Wahren-Herlenius asks, and does it favour Mojsov or Knudsen?
Does any member see a three-name configuration for B021 that is defensible on the documents, and does a tool-for-discovery prize need the clinical bar applied to B049 and B014?

Sandberg's statement refers to unease over conduct questions concerning one credited individual in the TOR ballot (B001), which is not described in the other five statements; can this be clarified from the evidence, or should it be set aside?
summary.chair_observation: All six members place B049 first and their configurations differ only in the third name, five choosing Mojsov and one Knudsen, so the live questions for round 2 are attribution and the discovery-versus-development standard rather than merit. B014 is the only other ballot named as an alternative by every member, with the Eshhar gap and Rosenberg's separate lineage as the main open points. Round 1 gives no explicit support for a second prize part from any member's preferred configuration.
